source.title: Do tabular foundation models repair themselves?

page_placements.theme: Self-repair after ablation is common but partial, and its size varies with model, data and training

record.file_problem: Some equations and inequality symbols are missing from the web text, but the reported results and model-to-value mappings are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study investigates layer-wise self-repair in tabular foundation models, but it does not test L10H7, copy suppression, or whether copy suppression contributes to self-repair. Its results concern a related, broader question rather than a version of the claim.
record.gate_note: The study measures total and direct effects of layer ablations in tabular foundation models. It reports these broader self-repair results under fits_no_version; it does not measure the claimed head, token suppression, calibration, or copy-suppression self-repair mechanism. Results attributed to McGrath et al. and Balef et al. are cited work and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures layer-wise self-repair (total vs direct effect under resample ablation) in four tabular foundation models. It does not study GPT-2 small, L10H7, attention heads, copy suppression, calibration, or copy suppression's share of self-repair. Its results concern a related but different question (whether self-repair exists at all in TFMs), so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find weak evidence of layer-wise self-repair in four TFMs, with redundancy more prevalent, and call for more models, tasks and datasets. They add that the mechanism behind near-zero total effects remains unclear.
record.recipe_differences: Uses layer-level causal total/direct-effect measurements, resample ablation, and correct-label logit margins in tabular models; it does not analyze the original study's attention-head copy-suppression method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported repair proportions and fitted diagnostics differ across the four tested models.

fits_no_version.finding: In four tabular foundation models on 15 binary TabArena tasks, few dataset-layer points fall in the authors' 'repaired' region (0–11%). Redundancy is more common (16–78%). The best-fitting CE-vs-DE layers show near-zero R² or negative slopes, unlike Chinchilla 7B (slope 0.69, R² 0.92).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-wise self-repair (Hydra-effect style) is weak in the tested tabular foundation models, and redundancy explains robustness to layer ablation better.

record.problems: The authors note that the study covers a limited number of models and datasets and only binary classification. The web text omits some equation symbols, including the inequalities defining the region categories. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the study's own reported results. The Chinchilla 7B and Balef et al. results are cited from other work and are not extracted as this study's results.

untested.parts: Not studied: GPT-2 small, L10H7, or token suppression.
No QK/OV circuit analysis and no loss attribution.
No upstream copier ablation and no copy-suppression mechanism; only layer-level self-repair in TFMs.
No negative heads examined in any model.
Does not decompose self-repair into copy suppression versus other sources such as LayerNorm. It only tests whether layer-level repair is present at all, in tabular models.

record.verdict_notes: No instructions in text. The Chinchilla 7B reference row in the table is a cited result and is correctly excluded from the rows. The inequality definitions of the regions are missing from the web text, so the redundant/repaired thresholds cannot be checked. None of this affects the claim versions.

versions.untested_parts: Does not study GPT-2 small L10H7, token copying, or the head's role across a training distribution.
Does not analyze L10H7's QK or OV circuits or measure their contribution to loss.
Does not test copy suppression or model calibration.
Does not ablate an upstream copier or measure copy suppression as a self-repair mechanism.
Does not test whether negative heads in other models or tasks implement copy suppression.
Does not compare copy suppression with other sources of self-repair or estimate copy suppression's share of self-repair.

relation.reason: It discusses related self-repair research but provides no test or operational use of the catalog's copy-suppression claims.

tranche.reason: The study measures layer-wise self-repair and redundancy in tabular foundation models, without testing or using copy suppression or measuring its contribution to self-repair.

source_check.notes: Region-defining inequalities and some mathematical headings are missing from the extraction, but reported proportions and fit values remain identifiable. The authors' cautious conclusion is accurately paraphrased; these results do not establish any copy-suppression verdict.
